source.title: Provable Super-Convergence With a Large Cyclical Learning Rate

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; figure values are not numerically readable in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes and demonstrates unstable cyclical learning rates on linear regression and strongly convex objectives, conceptually testing recovery under learning rates above the stability limit. It does not test wide neural networks.
record.gate_note: The neural-network Hessian and Jacobian observations are cited prior work, not results of this study. The study's own plotted comparison is on a linear regression task with a bimodal Hessian spectrum.
record.test_reason: The study proves convergence for a deliberately alternating learning-rate schedule on linear regression and strongly convex objectives. It does not test V5's neural-network dynamics: recovery through falling curvature, sharpness tracking the stability threshold, or divergence despite starting below it. Neural-network observations are cited or proposed as possible extensions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish rapid convergence for a two-value cyclical schedule under bimodal-Hessian assumptions, with an additional cross-smoothness restriction for nonlinear objectives. They leave broader theoretical extensions and further practical empirical validation to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a periodic two-value schedule with one unstable step and several stable steps, and proves convergence for linear regression and a class of strongly convex functions; it does not run neural-network experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The claimed acceleration depends on a bimodal Hessian spectrum with small local condition numbers; the nonlinear theorem also requires sufficiently small cross-smoothness.

fits_no_version.finding: For bimodal quadratic Hessians, periodically combining one unstable step with sufficiently many stable steps yields convergence whose iteration complexity scales as κ+κ− log(κ) log(1/accuracy). Figure 1 illustrates the advantage as κ increases. Theorem 2 extends the guarantee to strongly convex objectives with sufficiently small cross-smoothness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A carefully chosen cyclical learning-rate schedule can accelerate optimization of objectives with clustered Hessian spectra despite including individually unstable steps.

record.problems: The empirical comparison is only a linear regression task and the plotted values cannot be recovered from the supplied text. Practical neural-network validation is explicitly left for future work.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. Figure 1 compares gradient descent and Nesterov AGD as well as unstable CLR, but the supplied text provides no separately recoverable values for those comparator curves.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks, including corrupted labels and model-size or regularization comparisons.
Spurious minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-related training degradation and its prevention through shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth.

All stated neural-network phenomena: above-threshold recovery with falling curvature, divergence at larger rates, sharpness tracking the stability threshold, and divergence from initially subthreshold rates.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V5 labels. Evidence about a different objective class and a compensating cyclical schedule neither supports nor limits the stated neural-network claim. The row states indicate inability to assess the claim versions, not failure of the reported linear-regression convergence.

versions.untested_parts: No classification benchmarks, random-label experiments, or network size sweep.
No teacher-student ReLU problem or width comparison.

Tests unstable cyclical learning rates on linear regression, not wide neural networks. Does not test a brief loss rise with curvature drop, sharpness hovering at a stability threshold, or divergence from below the threshold.
